speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if the double vision and weakness fluctuate throughout the day, perhaps worsening as the day progresses? Also, do you experience any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the double vision or weakness improve after taking a short rest, and have you noticed any ptosis or drooping of your eyelids? Also, do you have any difficulty swallowing or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of the eyelids or double vision that worsens when you look upward? I also need to know if you have any difficulty swallowing or slurring when you speak.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me check your reflexes and perform a bedside ice pack test to see if your eyelid drooping improves with cold. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine receptor antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
